newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico hardliner denies leading powerful group.
newsitem.headline: Mexico hardliner denies leading powerful group.

text.p: A powerful Mexican ruling party politician denied on Wednesday he was the leader of a group of "dinosaurs" seeking to turn back the clock on President Ernesto Zedillo's political and economic reforms.
Manuel Bartlett, governor of Puebla state, told a meeting of women journalists that newspaper claims he headed a "governors' union" pressuring Zedillo were false.
"It would, perhaps be very useful because we could strengthen ourselves but there is no governors' union," he said. "I don't think I represent any group in particular."

Mexican commentators frequently mention Bartlett, a former Interior Minister and Education Minister, as a leader of the hardline group of politicians within the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
Known for his virulent attacks on the opposition, Bartlett is adored by many of the PRI's rank-and-file members, who see him as a strong leader who could restore the party's fortunes.

Asked about the PRI's dinosaurs and their ideology, Bartlett said sarcastically: "Is talking about social justice a sign of dinosaurism? We have to reflect what is the modern posture today and what is retrograde ... You can be a nationalist without being against what is modern".
Bartlett said corruption allegations and political errors had left the PRI in a weak position "but we hope to strengthen ourselves very soon".

Bartlett is best known for his supervision of the 1988 presidential election, which was won by Carlos Salinas under circumstances which most Mexicans believe were fraudulent. Bartlett has repeatedly denied any irregularities in the election.
